title: Forward decoding of a paired field
statement: Let $x$ and $w$ be bit words, let $p$ be an input-head position among the $|x|+2$ positions, and let $\mathrm{pre},\mathrm{tail},\mathrm{written},\mathrm{old}$ be bit words. Starting with the reader in its initial control state, with stream $\mathrm{pre}\,\langle w,\mathrm{tail}\rangle$ and target $\mathrm{written}\,\mathrm{old}$, after $2|w|$ steps its stream and control state are unchanged, while the target is $\mathrm{written}\,w\,\mathrm{drop}_{|w|}(\mathrm{old})$. The stream cursor has advanced from $|\mathrm{pre}|$ to $|\mathrm{pre}|+2|w|$, and the target cursor from $|\mathrm{written}|$ to $|\mathrm{written}|+|w|$.
hypotheses_covered: $p$ is a valid input-head position among the $|x|+2$ positions
replaced: For every input word, input position, field word $w$, stream prefix, stream tail, written target prefix, and old suffix, running the reader for $2|w|$ steps decodes all of $w$ into the target, one overwritten cell per decoded bit, preserves the exact unread stream suffix, and leaves the separator for the following steps; both stream bits of each pair are charged individually.
